But several claims are not supported by the cited claims or the card, and one cited claim ID does not exist in the packet. The next steps are generic and don't match the rationale's own recommendation.","problems":["Cited claim C0059971 does not exist in the card; the card has C0059971 only as... actually the card lists C0059971 as a 99215 with COPD, age 70, so the ID is valid, but the ID in the example differs from the rationale's cited IDs, which is inconsistent.","Rationale says presentations such as 'rash' and 'follow-up visits' for the low-complexity sample, but no rash dx appears on the card (dx are J06.9, M54.50, R21, Z09, R10.9). C0060461 is R21, which is a rash code, and Z09 is a follow-up code, so this is partly defensible, but the 'rash' label is an inference.","'Roughly double the all-provider rate in every band' is overstated: bands range from about 1.5x to 2.4x, e.g. 0.143 vs 0.059 and 0.348 vs 0.136 are above double, while 0.455 vs 0.234 and 0.183 vs 0.09 are around 2x. It is mostly fair but loose.","Headline calls it a 'strong screening signal' while the leaning is inconclusive and the z-score vs peers is only 0.68; this weakens the tone and is not reconciled with the low peer z-score.","Calls the low-complexity pattern 'consistent with upcoding', which is less cautious than ideal given there is no documentation for any 99215.","The rationale recommends requesting records for the sampled low-complexity 99215 claims and a high-complexity comparison set, but the coded next_steps only say to request a larger sample of 99214/99215 claims and re-screen, which is generic and does not name claim IDs.","The 'Examples' include C0061480 (a 99214), which does not illustrate the 99215 concern; the other examples are only age and chronic-condition counts."]}
